run.question: We got a customer complaint about slow response times in Europe. The customer mentioned seeing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 in their error page. Find what happened with this request and which service had the issue.

report.summary: The request ID belongs to a failed authentication call. The only record for REQ-EU-8K4M2 in the log store is an ERROR written by the auth service in region eu-west at 2026-11-18T16:49:47Z: endpoint /api/v2/auth/validate, response_time_ms 15847, user_id customer-39284, message 'Authentication request timeout - request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 took 15847ms to respond. LDAP backend connection pool exhausted. Customer authentication failed after retry attempts.' So the service that had the issue is auth (eu-west), and its own error text attributes the 15.8 s response to an exhausted LDAP backend connection pool. Same-day comparisons show auth in eu-central, ap-northeast, ap-south, us-east and us-west logging 'Request completed successfully' at 150 ms, all 27 other eu-west services logging 150 ms successes at 19:26Z, and eu-west auth itself logging a 150 ms success at 19:26Z about 2h37m after the error, so the failure was not a regional platform failure and the service recovered. Across the entire 1620-index log corpus only this one ERROR record exists and the string LDAP appears only in it. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable for every query, and the reachable Kubernetes cluster contains no auth workload, so error rate/frequency, trace corroboration and auth pod-level state are unverified; the underlying LDAP backend's own state is not observable in any available source.

claims.text: The only record matching REQ-EU-8K4M2 is in index app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05 with @timestamp 2026-11-18T16:49:47Z, service=auth, region=eu-west, level=ERROR, endpoint=/api/v2/auth/validate, response_time_ms=15847, request_id=REQ-EU-8K4M2, user_id=customer-39284.

That auth record's message is exactly 'Authentication request timeout - request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 took 15847ms to respond. LDAP backend connection pool exhausted. Customer authentication failed after retry attempts.', i.e. the auth service itself reports an exhausted LDAP backend connection pool behind the 15847 ms auth timeout and failed customer authentication after retries.

Baseline for the same service: eu-west auth logged INFO 'Request completed successfully' at 150 ms on 2026-11-14, 11-15, 11-16 and 11-17 at 19:26Z, again at 2026-11-18T19:26:00Z (after the error), and on 2026-11-19 through 2026-11-23 at 19:26Z, so 150 ms is its normal sampled latency and it was back to normal on the same day as the incident.

On 2026-11-18 auth logged INFO 150 ms 'Request completed successfully' in ap-northeast, ap-south, eu-central, us-east and us-west at 19:26:00Z, and the eu-west auth sample at the same time was also 150 ms, so other regions' auth was not failing in this corpus.

Every other eu-west service record on 2026-11-18 (analytics, api, cache, cart, catalog, checkout, db, inventory, notification, orders, payments, pricing, profiles, promotions, ratings, recommendations, reviews, search, shipping, subscriptions, tracking, users, web, wishlist, worker, billing) is INFO 'Request completed successfully' with response_time_ms 150 at 19:26:00Z; the auth ERROR at 16:49:47Z is the only non-INFO eu-west record that day.

A match_all query for 2026-11-18T16:00-17:30Z across all 1620 indices returned only this one auth ERROR document, and an aggregation over the eu-west 2024.01.05 indices for that window bucketed only service 'auth' with 1 document, 1 error and max/avg response_time_ms 15847.

A level=ERROR search over the whole authorized window across all 1620 app-185-* indices (0 failed shards) returned exactly one document, this auth record; the index listing shows 1620 indices and none outside the app-185-* family (non_app185_count 0), so this was the only ERROR log in the entire available log corpus.
The string LDAP occurs in exactly one document in the whole log corpus: this eu-west auth ERROR record.

The reachable Kubernetes cluster has no auth workload: its 24 deployments, 29 services and 32 running pods are only otel-demo (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, jaeger, kube-state-metrics, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, product-catalog, prometheus, prometheus-readonly-proxy, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart, alertmanager) plus kube-system and local-path-storage objects; none is named auth.

The only Kubernetes events in the authorized window are 4 Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint events on Endpoints with source timestamps 18:29:58-19:12:19 on 2026-11-23, about five days after the request; no pod crash, eviction or OOM event was returned.

The mechanism was saturation of the auth service's own LDAP connection pool, so the /api/v2/auth/validate call waited ~15.8 s and then failed after retries; whether the LDAP backend itself was slow, shedding connections or simply overloaded by request volume cannot be verified because no LDAP backend logs, metrics or objects exist in the available sources.

The impact was not region-wide or platform-wide in the observed data: eu-central auth and auth in four other regions logged 150 ms successes on 2026-11-18, and all 27 other eu-west services logged 150 ms successes that day; however the corpus stores about one log record per service per day per index, so the absence of further error records is also consistent with sparse sampling rather than proven isolation.

A crash, eviction, OOM or other Kubernetes workload fault in the available cluster was considered as the cause and rejected: no auth workload exists in that cluster at all, all its pods are Running, and its only events are Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint warnings five days after the request.

For the auth service in eu-west, obtain LDAP connection-pool metrics (active/idle/waiting, acquisition timeouts) and LDAP server-side health for 2026-11-18T16:49Z, and add an alert on pool saturation and on auth /validate latency; also confirm which component rendered the customer's error page, since no web/api error record exists for this request.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for every query (execute_prometheus_instant_query sum(traces_span_metrics_calls_total), get_label_values on service_name for traces_span_metrics_calls_total/http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, list_prometheus_rules) returning SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency or pool metric was available and it is unknown whether auth even has series in Prometheus.

Jaeger was unreachable (traces_list_services and traces_search for frontend 2026-11-18T16:30-17:10Z both SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so the request's trace, span timings and call chain could not be inspected or corroborated.

No LDAP backend telemetry exists in the available sources: no LDAP logs, metrics, namespace or object were found, so why the auth LDAP connection pool was exhausted, when saturation began and whether the LDAP directory itself was degraded are unknown.

The auth service is not a Kubernetes object in the reachable cluster (no auth deployment, pod or service), so its pod status, restarts, resource limits/requests, configuration and events could not be checked; the app-185 log corpus and the otel-demo cluster appear to be different environments.
No log record exists for the customer-facing error page: web and api in eu-west only logged INFO 150 ms successes at 19:26Z, so which component produced the error page the customer saw is unverified.

Pod logs for the incident window were unavailable: the frontend container retained only 10 lines, all after the requested window (read-through 2026-11-23T14:37Z), and no previous container instance existed.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no change or configuration event (e.g. pool-size change or LDAP failover) can be tied to the incident.

Only one request record (REQ-EU-8K4M2) exists in the log corpus, so the number of other affected requests, error rate and any customer-wide impact are unknown; the 1620-index corpus holds roughly one record per service per day.
next_steps: Obtain auth service LDAP connection-pool and /api/v2/auth/validate latency series from the auth platform's monitoring for 2026-11-18 16:00-18:00Z and compare with the preceding days.
Ask the LDAP/directory backend owners for their availability and connection-limit telemetry at 2026-11-18T16:49Z, and check whether pool sizing or an LDAP failover changed around that time.
Identify which tier (web/api/frontend) rendered the customer's error page for REQ-EU-8K4M2, since that tier has no error record in the log store.
Check whether other Europe (eu-west) customers hit the same auth timeout by querying the auth platform's raw logs rather than the sampled app-185 corpus.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
